details:
I've made an interactable that acts as a laser pointer (or wii remote) for a 'screen'.  It's in 'gun orientation' mode, so that desktop users can also participate.  However: the point that the interactable aims at the screen at, is slightly *offset* from the reticle that's always visible in desktop mode (by default), since the pointer in the user's hand is to one side of the player's camera rather than pointing straight out of their nose.  (The two 'beams' would meet at an infinitely far distance, but not a point a few feet in front of the player.)   This gives desktop users the confusing situation of seeing two 'cursors' simultaneously; the one glued to the middle of their window, and the one corresponding to where their pointer's beam hits the in-world screen, which is slightly offset from the middle of their window.

The ideal resolution for this would be if we could just access the native raycast for the user's cursor (their active hand in VR or their head on desktop), as suggested here: https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/expose-highlight-of-udon-interact so that this "second pointer" isn't necessary in the first place; but if that's too difficult, just being able to toggle the desktop reticle to reduce that confusion would be nice.
title: Let udon hide reticle while holding interactable
